extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.use_case: This application implements an agentic AI workflow for customer service in a travel context. It serves users by triaging and routing requests to specialized agents (FAQ, Flight Status, Seat Booking, Cancellation), and uses jailbreak and relevance guardrails to control interactions. The system operates exclusively on text input and output, with no support for voice, image, or video.
summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure via GitHub Actions
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** Deployment targets Azure but lacks evidence of multi-region or HA configuration; availability is unaddressed.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** GitHub Actions secrets
- **Credential handling:** Azure credentials are injected via `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` — a secret reference, not plaintext, but stored as a GitHub secret rather than a dedicated external vault.
- **Assessment:** Credentials are not stored in plaintext, but reliance on GitHub-managed secrets increases exposure surface compared to a dedicated secret management service.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not evidenced
- **Key management:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No encryption-at-rest coverage or key management information is available; this must be verified at the resource level.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** Managed identity referenced as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** IAM scope is `subscription`; trust is granted to `github-actions` principals. No granular role or resource-level scope is specified.
- **Assessment:** Subscription-scoped credentials violate least privilege; the scope should be narrowed to the minimum required resource group or resource.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** Runs on `ubuntu-latest`; triggers are `push` and `workflow_dispatch`.
- **OIDC / credential flow:** OIDC is not used (`uses_oidc: false`); long-lived Azure credentials are passed as secrets, increasing credential rotation risk.
- **Assessment:** Lack of OIDC means static credentials are used in the pipeline, which is less secure than token-based authentication with short-lived tokens.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No container-specific configuration is present; container security posture cannot be assessed from this data.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. **Implement OIDC** between GitHub Actions and Azure to replace long-lived credentials with short-lived tokens, reducing secret exposure.
2. **Reduce IAM scope** from `subscription` to the specific resource group or resource, enforcing least privilege.
3. **Add encryption-at-rest** configuration for all Azure resources, and document key management if using customer-managed keys.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Architecture & Orchestration**: FastAPI exposes four endpoints (Login, Me, Logout, Chat). All endpoints are protected by Bearer Auth. The Chat endpoint funnels requests through a Triage Agent, which delegates to specialized agents (Flight Status, FAQ, Cancellation, Seat Booking). All agents use the `gpt-4.1-mini` model.
- **Tool Access**: All agents (including Triage) have access to the same five tools: Baggage, Cancel Flight, Display Seat Map, Faq Lookup, and Flight Status. The OpenAI Agents framework can additionally call Lookup Reservation and Update Seat tools.
- **Guardrails**: Two guardrails (Relevance and Jailbreak) execute before agents act, both using `gpt-4.1-mini`. They cover the Chat endpoint but do **not** filter tool calls — any agent can invoke any tool regardless of context.
- **Risk Pattern – Over‑permissive agents**: Every agent can call every tool, including destructive ones like Cancel Flight. This violates least‑privilege; a misdirected FAQ agent could cancel a booking.
- **Datastore**: Sqlite is listed with no connections in this graph, suggesting it may be accessed implicitly by tools or is not mapped. Its exposure is unknown but a potential blind spot.
- **Sensitive operations**: Cancel Flight and Update Seat are unguarded post‑authorization — once past Bearer Auth, any agent can trigger them without additional checks.
